# the contributor audit: signed guard escape and support vacancy tests

PASS after reading all of candidate a78d27235a5a2dff, candidate 34860ded7f752276, and planar-two-cap-exposed-source-vacancy-and-affine-parity-span-independent.md.

For the replicated guards, select the actual menu capturing positive matching guards. The affine field sum z is zero on T and takes opposite values on identical reflected bodies. Total boundary mass and every covariance integral cancel. Capture response equals L times the guard perimeter. The finite path scaling positive and negative guards by sigma minus/plus t/r_T preserves their Minkowski averages and the exact central fiber. Extreme bases retain prescribed fibers. The mass and pooled covariance formulas have the correct even coefficients. All three test caps have the same strictly negative derivative. Their balanced normals cover every candidate point of the central fiber, and the exposed-guard gap persists. This proves actual maximum-depth descent, not just a chosen-center estimate.

For general polytope contact in n=1, concavity of actual support roofs and equality at -1,0 force every right fiber into the middle polytope. Eliminating the base tilt from two complete misses gives the reflected support bound with the full negative 2hGamma reserve. One bound below the support midpoint excludes base2 and all later integer fibers, justifying isolation. The final volume estimate is explicitly conditional; contact alone is not claimed to supply it.

For the planar triangle lemma, midpoint compatibility supplies the two nonnegative barycentric coordinates of the opposite candidate fiber. The actual misses bound their maxima by 2/3-sigma-2w_j. No third-coordinate restriction is presumed. The area Jacobian is 2V and marginal density bound is 2V alpha_k. Outward averaging adds mean displacement w_j/2, giving exactly V alpha_k(alpha_j+w_j)<4V/9. Exposure in the COMPLETE sampled hull is assumed or proved in the n=1 variant. No off-line mass is discarded in higher n.

Halving distance to aff(I) under parity-complete midpoint moves proves aff(I)=aff(P) by finiteness. This only obstructs affine rebates vanishing at every source. It does not supply a common multi-source separator or a Gamma capacity theorem.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
